newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns nations against ties with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China warns nations against ties with Taiwan.

text.p: China warned other countries on Thursday to be alert against attempts by Taiwan to break out of diplomatic isolation and boost its international standing.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang warned of possible damage to relations with China if countries that recognise Beijing sanction visits by Taiwanese government officials, and mentioned the United States by name.
"The Taiwan authorities...now are unceasingly taking opportunities to create two Chinas...in particular by visits to other countries," Shen told a news briefing.

Asked about overseas visits by Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan, currently travelling in Europe, Shen lashed out at the island that Beijing has regarded as a rebel province since the end of their civil war in 1949.

"Their purpose is very clear, they want to expand their international space and continue to engage in activites of 'two Chinas' or 'One China, One Taiwan,' he said, referring to what Beijing sees as a bid by Taiwan to move toward independence.
"So other countries should be on alert in this matter," he said, when asked about rumours that Lien was planning a visit to Ireland while in Europe.
"They should not damage relations with China because of the Taiwan issue," he said.

"I want to stress that recently the United States has sold weapons to Taiwan," he said, and alleged that the sale violated three Washington communiques with Beijing under which the United States pledged to gradually reduce weapons sales to Taiwan.
"This (sale) is not without links to Taiwan engaging in its 'two Chinas', 'One China, one Taiwan' activities," he said.

Taiwan took delivery on Wednesday of four launch vehicles for U.S.-made Patriot missiles, part of its drive to improve its defences in the face of China's army modernisation, Taiwan's United Evening News has reported.
It did not say when the Gulf War-tested Patriot anti-missile missiles themselves would be delivered.
Washington switched diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei in 1979.
A private visit by Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui to the United States in June 1995 sent Sino-U.S. relations into a tailspin from which they have begun to recover only recently.

Beijing has sought to push Taiwan into diplomatic isolation in its quest to bring the island under its rule. Taiwan has responded with trips -- open or secret -- by its leaders to countries that recognise Beijing but not Taipei.
